title: gate-chain/1 — checks between a method's output and what ships
description: An ordered list of gates the eval engine applies to every translated segment before it is scored or shipped (mt-eval run / test / translate --gates). People bring their own gates (founder, 2026-10-10): a gate of kind metric-threshold reads one per-segment value from a metric plugin — any plugin the harness loads, e.g. an FST validity check — and compares it with min and/or max. The first gate that refuses a segment decides what ships instead: drop (nothing), keep-source (the source text), flag (the output, marked) or fallback (the chain's fallback method's translation, if the gates accept it — else nothing). A segment the plugin cannot score is refused (no value). What is measured is what ships: the headline scores the gated output, the ungated score is reported beside it, and the refusal rate is a number of its own. Retrying a refused segment with the gate's reason comes later.

fallback.description: What translates a segment a gate refuses with on_refuse fallback: a method that runs on this machine (a dictionary: lexicon; a model: local-model), so nothing leaves it. Its output is checked by the same gates; refused again, nothing ships. For serving and translating only: a command that scores (mt-eval run / test) refuses a chain that falls back, because the score would be partly this method's and partly the fallback's under one name (founder, 2026-10-11) — measure the fallback as a method of its own.

model.description: The dictionary (lexicon) or model (local-model) it runs.

field.description: The key in the plugin's per-segment result (a number, or true/false read as 1/0).

min.description: Refuse a segment whose value is below this.

max.description: Refuse a segment whose value is above this.
